feature: A frame can be the size of an icon
summary: New Frame now offers the sizes icons are drawn at, 16 through 512, under the five screens. Pick one and the canvas takes you there at a zoom you can actually draw at, so a 24 pixel icon opens as a square the size of your hand instead of a speck.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. The flag is "Make a frame the size of an icon" and it is on by default.

try.do: Open a blank document, then choose Layer and New Frame.
Click 24 in the Icons row, then Add Frame.
Draw an ellipse inside the frame you land on.
Click the empty white beside the ellipse to pick the frame, and read the Size row in the panel.
Choose Layer and New Frame again, and notice 24 is still the one lit.
Open the Experiments window, turn "Make a frame the size of an icon" off, and open New Frame again: the five screens are back and the Icons row is gone.

evaluate: Landing at 3200% for a 24 pixel canvas: is that where you wanted to be, or would you rather arrive further out and zoom in yourself?
The icon sizes are a row of buttons and the screens are a list of rows. Does that read at a glance, or should the icons be rows like everything else?
The screens have no heading and the icons do. Does the asymmetry bother you?
Is 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 512 the right six, or is something you actually draw at missing?
Drawing a 14 pixel dot at 3200%, did the canvas feel precise or slippery?
rough: The camera only moves for New Frame. Pressing F and clicking once also drops a frame at the last size picked, and that one leaves the camera where it was, so a 24 pixel frame dropped that way really is a speck. It felt wrong to move the canvas under a tool you are holding, but it is a real inconsistency.

A second frame is placed to the RIGHT of the ones already there, and past a point that is off the canvas, which the camera cannot scroll to. Reproduced with two plain Desktop screens, so it has nothing to do with icon sizes; filed as "A second screen lands where the canvas cannot follow it".

Nothing about the icon here knows it is an icon: no keylines, no live area, no snapping to whole pixels, no preview at size. That was deliberate, the task was narrowed to the canvas alone, but the mock at docs/design/mocks/pages/icon-draw-wt.html is mostly about the grid, so what shipped is the floor of that page and not the page.

Where the mock was not followed: it draws a 24 unit artboard with a 20 by 20 live area and calls that the icon canvas. A frame here is just 24 by 24 pixels with nothing drawn on it. The live area is part of the keylines slice, not this one.

A shape drawn in a 24 pixel frame gets the app's ordinary 4 pixel default border, which at icon scale is a sixth of the whole canvas. Not changed here, but somebody drawing icons will meet it immediately.
